text:
mira: Hey team — SignalFlare POC hit intermittent 429s from our hosted endpoint when running through their corp proxy. They're running both TS SDK and Python clients. Can someone help triage? (trial expires EOW) :eyes:
alex: tagging. Do we have logs from their side or a request id? quick reproduce steps?
sam: saw the 429s in our rate logs — spikes from a single IP range, looks bursty. Not a platform-wide rate limit, more like connection reuse issues behind proxy.
mira: customer sent a snippet and a curl response:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 15:01:12 GMT
x-request-id: rf-17a2b5
ratelimit-remaining: 0
ratelimit-reset: 12
```
mira: they also attached Node and Python client stacks. Node app uses `node-fetch` inside a lambda-ish container; python uses `requests.Session()` on EC2 behind corporate proxy.
alex: common culprits: proxy not supporting keep-alive / connection pooling gets reset -> TCP handshake per request -> proxy throttles -> 429 from infra or proxy. Also TLS handshake timeouts can surface.
sam: can we see their sdk headers? We add a header `x-rw-retry: n` for tracing but not sure if they used SDK retry config.
mira: they say they used default SDK settings. TS sample they provided:
```js
await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'redwood/gpt-lite', input: '...' })
```
no custom agent.
jeff: quick checklist:
- ensure HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env is set in container correctly
- for node, set an https.Agent with keepAlive: true
- for python, mount a requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter with pool_connections & pool_maxsize
- add exponential backoff + jitter in client retry (avoid hammering proxy)
alex: propose quick fix for TS (copy to customer):
```js
import https from 'https';
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 100 });
const client = new Redwood({ fetchOptions: { agent, timeout: 20000, retry: { retries: 6, minTimeout: 200 } } });
```
mira: python snippet for them:
```py
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
s = requests.Session()
retries = Retry(total=5, backoff_factor=0.3)
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=20, pool_maxsize=50, max_retries=retries))
resp = s.post(url, json=payload, timeout=20)
```
alex: also ask them to set `NO_PROXY` for our internal health probe endpoints if they're routing through a proxy that strips headers.
sam: we can also flip on per-client slower rate-limits on our side for this trial account to avoid 429s while they stabilize.
karen: (from sales) If we throttle less, does that affect billing/abuse controls? Customer wants to finish POC this week and has a pricing Q: extra test tokens/extended trial?
alex: I can approve a temporary soft-rate-limit bump for the POC account for 72h. Will log an exception. k
mira: security asked if they can accept the security questionnaire now — they need SOC2 doc and network/IP ranges for the dedicated option.
jeff: I have SOC2 link ready, sending via S3 link to them. For IP ranges, we can provide our public egress CIDR and dedicated pool options. @mira will follow up.
mira: sending the TS + Py fixes to customer now. Also asked them to capture a packet-level log or proxy-connect logs to confirm keepalive behavior.
customer_ops: (customer) quick update — applied the node agent changes, still saw a 429 but much less frequent. Attached stack trace and snippet showing `ECONNRESET` to proxy around same time.
sam: ECONNRESET from proxy + bursts -> likely proxy health checks or connection limits. Two immediate asks:
1) try setting `Connection: keep-alive` explicitly
2) increase SDK retry/backoff to spread retries
alex: I'll open a support escalation to infra to look at our edge logs for rf-17a2b5 and similar request ids in that window.
infra-bot: New ticket created: INF-2197 for edge-rate-analysis (refs: rf-17a2b5). Assigned to @sam.
sam: analyzing — preliminary: multiple clients reuse a small connection pool causing serialized requests when proxy drops sockets. Recommend customer raise pool sizes and our soft bump to be permanent for trial.
mira: sales asked about pricing if they go dedicated after POC — @karen can you own follow-up? they want committed throughput numbers.
karen: will set up a scoping call tomorrow with capacity numbers and pricing tiers. also confirm we can share pricing sheet.
alex: followups:
- mira: confirm customer applied the NO_PROXY / agent changes (done)
- sam: keep infra ticket running and share edge timeline
- karen: schedule pricing review
mira: customer confirms Node agent + NO_PROXY fixed 90% of errors — only occasional 429 during long batch runs. They asked for final checklist and next steps to avoid enterprise blockers (SAML SSO, SOC2 link, contract lawyer).
jeff: checklist to send:
- SDK keepAlive + pool config examples (TS/Py)
- NO_PROXY recommendations
- temporary POC soft rate bump window (72h) + option to extend
- SOC2 report link + contact for security Qs
- Dedicated capacity IP ranges + contract sales owner
mira: awesome. I'll bundle and send. thanks everyone :pray:
karen: noted — will run scoping and contract thread after POC green.
mira: closing thread once I send the bundle. thanks :tada:
